So this framework is three levels. We're going to just call it the operating system. This operating system is three levels: Level 1, Level 2, Level 3.
So Level 1 is the foundational level. This is the basic level. This is the level that you literally have to have mostly handled to really be effective at the next levels. So Level 1 is your fuel, how well you move, and how well you rest. Fuel, movement, and rest—FMR for short. We'll just say that. Level 1: FMR—fuel, movement, and rest.
So fuel is what you're eating, what you're putting into your body, the actual energy that you're putting into your body. How are you making those choices? What are you eating? What are you doing? How are you doing it? Fuel.
Movement is your activity throughout the day. How often do you move your body? What are you doing? Are you running? Are you walking? Are you going upstairs? Are you taking elevators? Are you being lazy? Are you sitting a lot? What's your movement like? Our bodies are built on movement, really. When we look at our brains, we have to have this movement to stimulate firing of neurons. You just stand up, you run in place for 10 seconds and sit down, you're going to think clearer. It's because movement is absolutely foundational. Level 1: foundational.
So we have fuel, we have movement, and then we have rest. So you put the energy in—cool, you got some energy. What are you going to use the energy for? Well, you're going to use it to move, and to do things, and to be active. When you're moving and you're doing things and you're being active, eventually you have to rest, because rest is where growth happens. It's where our brain can take a break, process memories. It's where our body has a breather from moving and can rebuild. 75% of our growth hormone is put into the system naturally, from the inside, while we sleep.
So, foundational principle, foundational level of the operating system is fuel, movement, and rest.
So now you have the foundational generally done, or at least within an area in your mind where you don't feel like you're lacking.
Two, Level 2, is how well you're doing internally. I call it the internal level. How are you thinking? How are you processing things in your mind? Are you learning? Are you pushing yourself? Are you building new connections in your nervous system to become healthier, stronger, more cognitively stable, and more cognitively strong?

So Level 2 is thinking, learning, and connecting.
Once you get your process down where you're thinking well, you feel like you're grounded internally, now it's time to shift to external. Your external foundation, or the external...
Once you get Level 1—you get your foundation generally figured out—and you've worked on Level 2—you're thinking well, you're processing, you're challenging yourself, you're pushing yourself, you're connected—connected at the end of Level 2 leads right to Level 3. So now we're going to look externally.
So, what's your external world like? Are you getting out of the house? Are you engaging with others? Are you playing? Are you doing things to where you're just having fun? Play is a main component of Level 3.

[00:00] In this video I'm going to show you how to use intermittent fasting every day for the rest of your life in a way that is super simple. Not only that, we're going to build a bullet journal panel so that you can track this each day, watch for trends, and the bullet journal panel actually will do most of the thinking for you.

[00:23] I'm Dr. Craig Anderson. I'm a licensed chiropractic physician. I've been in patient care for 29 years and I'm still seeing patients full-time. I'm excited to share this with you. This is information that I think is mission critical for you to live a healthy life.

[00:43] Everyone at some point in their life tries to maintain the weight. Maybe the weight has increased some and you feel like you just got to get it back? Weight management is really part of life.

[00:57] I want to show you something that I've done off and on for decades. I've coached hundreds of patients one-on-one to actually use this program and I'm going to show you everything you need to know. There's nothing to be sold, there's nothing extra to buy. All you need is a pen, a journal, maybe a ruler to draw straight lines, and the desire to get on top of this part of your life.

[01:23] If you've done a diet before, chances are you have had some success in the diet and then over time you move away from the diet, and then at some point you gain the weight back.

[01:38] So I'm going to show you a system that I am quite proud of. I have done this myself for many years. I've coached almost a thousand individuals one-on-one through this exact plan.

[01:52] So before we get into the nuts and bolts of how you're going to journal this lifestyle change and how that journal is going to help you think through this every day, there's a few principles we need to understand. The first principle is yesterday's carbohydrates dictates today's hunger.

[02:14] So when you wake up in the morning, when you woke up this morning, you were hungry at some point in the day. At some point in the morning you got hungry. Did you get hungry early in the morning, mid-morning, or maybe you don't get hungry until lunchtime? That hunger signal in the morning really indicates how well you are burning carbohydrates and how well you're shifting from carbohydrate-burning mode to fat-burning mode.

[02:46] You need to be able to burn both of these fuels. If you can't burn fat, what's going to happen? Well, you're going to store fat easier. If you can't burn carbohydrates, then you got a bigger problem. It's called diabetes and it can be life-threatening. That's not the topic of this video. In this video, we're talking normal physiology in people that are healthy and teaching your body how to shift from the fat-burning mode and the carbohydrate-burning mode, and how to use that every day regardless of how you eat.

[03:22] Now, you're going to have to make some changes and when you have that motivation, when you have the mental energy to make those decisions and make good choices, do it. But sometimes you're not going to have that mental energy and you have to back-shift, you have to downshift a little bit. This system helps you see when that is.

[03:45] So yesterday's carbohydrates dictate in many ways when you get hungry today. So if you had a birthday cake at the end of the day, chances are you're going to wake up and you're going to feel a lot more hunger. And there's many reasons for that. There's several hormones in play here. We're not going to go into it too much, but just remember when you have a lot of carbohydrates, your insulin is going to jump up and that increased insulin can often shift gears to where you're not as close to burning fat when you go to bed. And so you wake up ready to eat. And essentially your body is saying, "Give me some carbohydrates. I want food, I want donuts, I want carbohydrates."

[04:30] So my game plan here is to retrain your body, retrain the physiology, retrain your metabolic pathways so that your body can burn carbs when you need to and you can get fuel from fat when you need to.

[04:47] One of the common concerns when we're looking at fasting is are you going to lose muscle? It's your body's natural response to not having enough calories to shift into muscle. There is some risk to that and we're going to mitigate for that risk. I'm going to show you how, and I think you're going to like that.

[05:07] A study recently came out in the journal Obesity looking at restricted eating and the overall metabolic impact. It showed that people doing a long-term caloric restricted diet, if they take 2 weeks off and just kind of eat normal food, not too crazy, but normal, the long-term weight loss is maintained much better. You have 55% more weight loss with intermittent fasting—you know, reducing your calories and then coming back and eating full calories back and forth—as compared to non-stop restricted caloric diet.

[05:46] So having a period of refeeding is protective for your metabolism and protective for your muscles.

[05:54] So we just have to plan for that. We just have to plan that we're going to have days where we're going to just eat a regular day. We're going to eat a full day. We're not going to be in caloric deficit. In fact, we might be a little bit in a in a caloric surplus. And that actually, my friends, is healthy.

[06:12] Let's now go to how do we journal this? How do we keep track of this? And as we go, I'm going to explain the plan, explain the process.

[06:23] Blank page, we are going to start the process of journaling this. Now, journaling, when you use an analog system, you are actually going to take a lot of the punitive feeling out of the diet. So if you're writing things down on paper, you don't have that app that's maybe telling you, "Hey, you failed! You're a failure!" It's just a piece of paper and a pen and you're just writing things. It has a psychological benefit that you're going to see as you go to this.

[06:56] So first, we're going to write "Fuel". We're going to make a panel, we're going to call it "Fuel".

[07:03] Now, if you really want to integrate it into your bullet journal, I'd go to your monthly panel and write down today as the first day of starting intermittent fasting. And "Fuel", this is on page 40, so we're going to go back and we're going to put a 40 next to it so we always know the date. It was April 2031, which is a made-up month or just a fictitious month, and "Fuel". So this is when we started fasting.

[07:34] I would recommend that you just use one side, basically a half panel, just to keep it all contained.

[07:44] So we're going to start out by drawing a line. Generally want to have a straight line. Don't really like the way it shifted off to the top there, but that's cool. We'll we'll go with it.

[07:55] No, actually, let's not go with it. Let's let's let's do another another page and and just start out right. Let's get this line nice and and straight.

[08:08] All right. So we're going to do this every day. So I want you to start by numbering each line for the day: the 1st of the month, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and so on. Go all the way down until you get to about an inch from the bottom. You're going to need to write a couple things on the bottom.

[08:29] And then in the way that we are using our journal, I'd recommend you also put the day of the week there: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. Just go down single digits and put the day of the week. This will help connect each of those days to kind of a greater greater week.

[08:48] Now, this first line, this is going to be the beginning of the day as far as time. So this first line is going to be a 6. That's 6:00 AM. Now, we're going to go in 3-hour increments. We're going to make the next line, we're going to put a 9 on top of that. Then the next line will be a 12. The next line will be a 3. Next line will be a 6, and the next line will be a 9 that represents 9:00 PM. So we're not going to really worry about anything outside of 6:00 AM and 9:00 PM. The reason is because you're not going to eat during those times. That's a non-eating time. But if you do eat, that's fine. The system can roll with it. I'll show you how that works.

[09:35] So I would put a double line right here just to show that, okay, this is different a different kind of data. This isn't a time scale that we're using here.

[09:46] Now we're going to have three additional columns. The first column will be for the window. We're going to write down the window of eating. This is when we are eating. The second column will be our carb level, so I'm just going to put "Carbs" there. Are we eating low carbs or regular carbs? We're not really going to shoot for high carbs, just so you know. The next one is "Mental," and then the next one is "Notes."

[10:14] Now, "Mental" is a subtle feeling of how you're doing mentally. Are you doing okay? Because at some point, if you push this too far mentally, you're going to feel like you've had enough and we're going to track that in the journal.

[10:33] On the bottom column between 9—I'm sorry, between 6 and 9, write down "12 Low." Between 9 and 12, write down "9 Low." And between 12 and 3, write down "9 / 6 Balanced."

[10:55] So this is going to be the fasting window you're going to do. Now, the secret sauce to this plan is when your morning hunger starts. So we talked about morning hunger as being a gauge on how you did the day before with your carbs. So this is it. This is this is the nugget. However you ate yesterday all summarizes and all comes down to a morning report card and that is your morning hunger.

[11:32] Let's say the first day of the week, the first day of the month, Monday the 1st, you wake up and you're feeling hunger around 7:30 or so, maybe 8:00. So you put a line right there around the 7:00, 8:00 period. And because that hunger started between 6 and 9, you go to the bottom and it says "12 Low." So we're going to do a 12-hour eating window and we're going to be low on the carbohydrates. We're going to try to reduce carbohydrates.

[12:08] And so that does not mean you're going to measure your carbs, you're going to measure all your calories. It just means you're going to lean away from carbohydrates. You're going to lean away from bread, you're going to lean away from the desserts, and you're going to just lean away from that. You're still going to eat generally the things that you normally eat. But if you normally have some extra cookies after dinner, skip the cookies. You're going to be low on your carbohydrate intake today because your hunger started pretty early.

[12:38] So after you've done a nice day of reducing the carbs a little bit over that 12-hour window, you wake up and you're not quite as hungry. The hunger starts at maybe 8:30 in the morning. Okay, good. Well, you're still in that first 3-hour window, so you're going to just do it again. You're going to have a 12-hour day where you're going to try to reduce carbs.

[12:59] Now, what this is doing: it's naturally retraining the machinery inside your cells to be able to get to the fat in your body. If you go too fast, it's going to shock the system. Now, you can get results, you can get quick weight loss results, but I'm telling you, it's going to come back pretty fast.

[13:20] So you go day after day and you track when your hunger starts. If your hunger starts in the 9:00 to 12:00 hour, okay, now you're shifting gears a little bit. That's telling us that your body's able to tap into some of the fat storage at night time and you don't wake up with extreme hunger. That hunger around 9:00, 9:30, we're going to put a line there and we're going to slide down and now we see that our fasting window today is 9 hours. Slide out 9 hours, put a line 9 hours later, and that's when you're going to end eating.

[13:58] Now as you're going through, you get to the point where you wake up and you're not really hungry. And so you have some water, have your coffee, and you just kind of don't worry about eating. You don't eat until you're hungry. Once you get hunger, then that's when you eat. And if that hunger goes all the way to let's say noon or 1:00, then you know that those little organs in your cells, those little organelles in your cells, the mitochondria, now can actually process fat. And so you're starting to use fat, and when you're using the fat, it causes satiation. You're not as hungry, so you don't wake up with as much hunger.

[14:41] This is something that you can just simply do every day. Now if you look off to the right: the window, that makes sense; the carbohydrates, that makes sense, you just bring it over each day. But then there is "Mental."

[14:58] So each day, I want you to put a an arrow up if you're, "Hey, I'm great! I'm feeling great. I'm up today." Put a sideways arrow if you're like, "Eh, just kind of flat, just I'm just it's fine. I'm okay. Everything's fine, but yeah, I'm good." Put a downward arrow if you're, "I'm just feeling down. I'm feeling maybe a little little depressed, a little more anxious, maybe a little more moody."

[15:23] And here's the rule I want you to remember. You might just write this down in the journal: if you have three downward arrows, increase your eating window and add a little bit of carbohydrates in there. Do that the next day to simply calibrate, calibrate, calibrate. Just every day you just calibrate to that morning hunger. If you continue to have those downward arrows, add a little more carb.

[15:53] Now, if you have clinical depression or anxiety, you're going to have to calibrate kind of your normal state on where you are and do the best you can there. This is really a measuring stick on how well energy is getting to your brain. If you start to get anxious or fatigued or just feeling more kind of melancholy, then we're starting to see a trend that we don't want. Let's back-calibrate the window, width the length of the window, to where you have a little more calories.

[16:29] Now, these small little tweaks can actually make it to where this can just be something you do for the rest of your life. [17:05] That's how you do it. That's how you implement this daily intermittent fasting tracking process. This process works. For men, it works easier than women. That is just the physiology difference between men and women.

[17:23] So if you're a man, you can expect 3 or 4 weeks of doing this, you'll naturally have less hunger in the morning time. If you're a woman, it may be a little bit longer. It may be more 4 to 6 weeks. I've taken women who are post-menopausal, pre-menopausal, young, old; men who are old, young, all different ages. [17:58] So the moral of the story here is you just simply have to stick with it and try not to worry about it too much.

[18:05] When you wake up in the morning, when are you hungry? That dictates your day. Then go about your day. If you have an event where you have to eat pizza that night, eat the pizza. That's fine. What you're doing here is you're establishing a habit to last your entire life and you want a life with pizza! You don't want to say, "Hey, I don't I don't eat pizza anymore." No, you don't want to be that person. You want to be able to enjoy life, you want to be able to socialize and engage. And if you're that person who has a special diet, that's that's fine, but it's going to kind of get old.

[18:43] I want you to feel like you are a healthy individual and you're somebody who can eat whatever you want to eat, but there are limits and there are gauges and there are ways that you track this so that you can manage your weight as well, and you can manage your overall health, and you can manage your overall energy state.

**Biological Reframe:** When you try to remember every task, email, and obligation, you fill up your working memory—your cognitive cache. This slows down your ability to process and be present.
